stories.notes: Empty acceptance criteria and null spec for a complex, multi-platform CMS live-preview feature. Openspec must elaborate requirements and define ACs first; speckit then hardens for testability, iframe/XSS security, real-time edge cases, and cross-platform (GO/UP/MX) coverage gaps.

agentContributions.notes: The Contentstack Stack initialization in src/services/contentstack.ts lacks the live_preview config key, preventing the SDK from connecting to the preview endpoint and resolving preview tokens. This is a configuration defect, not a novel feature — the SDK already supports live_preview; we just don't pass it.

Openspec provided an empty acceptanceCriteria array with a useful note identifying this as a configuration defect. I built the full AC set from scratch based on the story title, file paths, and openspec's note. Key design decisions: (1) AC-1/AC-2 cover the happy path and backward compatibility — the two most critical outcomes. (2) AC-3 and AC-6 cover edge cases for invalid tokens and API errors — without file contents I inferred these from the SDK's expected behavior; the implementer should validate against the actual SDK error surface. (3) AC-4 addresses security/caching — preview content must never be cached at the CDN layer. (4) AC-5 ensures cross-site consistency since the story explicitly scopes GO, UP, MX. (5) AC-7 ensures no secrets are baked into the build. (6) AC-8 validates end-to-end rendering through the component layer (useContent hook, ContentstackLink) listed in the technical notes. CAVEAT: I did not have access to the file contents of src/services/contentstack.ts, src/interface/content/contentCard.ts, src/components/contentstack/ContentstackLink/ContentstackLink.tsx, or src/hooks/useContent.ts. If the actual SDK initialization signature, query patterns, or component props differ from my assumptions, some ACs may need adjustment — particularly AC-8 which assumes the hook/component layer surfaces preview content transparently.

coordinatorReview.reviewNotes: Both agents added meaningful, non-overlapping value. Openspec identified the root cause with precision: the Contentstack SDK initialization in src/services/contentstack.ts is missing the live_preview config key — a configuration defect, not a greenfield feature. This is an actionable technical diagnosis that directly guides the implementer. Speckit then constructed a comprehensive verification-criteria set from scratch (happy path, backward compatibility, invalid tokens, API errors, CDN caching/security, cross-site GO/UP/MX consistency, secrets, end-to-end rendering through the hook/component layer). The two contributions are complementary: openspec says what is broken, speckit says what correct looks like. No overlap, no redundancy. All four manifest paths are confirmed to exist across all three codelines (gotransit, upexpress, metrolinx) with exact matches and zero unresolved entries — no missing_manifest_path flag. The file set is plausible for a live-preview change: SDK init (contentstack.ts), content interface (contentCard.ts), component (ContentstackLink.tsx), and hook (useContent.ts) cover the full stack from service through rendering. Speckit's caveat about not having file contents is noted but is not a scoring defect per policy. Remaining open questions (actual SDK error surface, hook/component transparency for preview content) are ordinary implementation-time concerns. Verification criteria are observable and testable.
